subject: Banking
title: Identity Theft and Credit Fraud
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Identity Theft and Credit Fraud.

hook.text: Every 22 seconds, someone in the US becomes a victim of identity theft.

buildup.text: Thieves open credit cards, take out loans, and file tax returns using stolen identities.

discovery.text: The dark web sells complete identity kits — name, SSN, address, and mother's maiden name — for as little as $15.

twist.text: Victims bear the burden of proof. You must prove you didn't open the account.

climax.text: Identity theft is cheap to commit and expensive to fix. The criminal profits quickly; the victim suffers for years.

punchline.text: $15 on the dark web buys a full identity. Victims spend months recovering.

quiz.question: How much does a stolen identity cost on the dark web?
